title: Final fields and varargs through reflection

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Reflection gets a private static final field, calls setAccessible(true) and then set(null, newValue). What happens?

options.text: The set succeeds, but code that reads the constant still sees the old value.
options.says: That is the story for an instance final field holding a compile-time constant; a static final field refuses the write itself.

options.text: The set throws IllegalAccessException, even though access was lifted before.
options.says: setAccessible does not make a static final field writable: Field.set throws IllegalAccessException, as it does for record fields.

options.text: The set succeeds, and every later read sees the new value at once.
options.says: A static final field cannot be modified through Field.set at all, whatever the access flag says.

questions.stem: Method m is the static method join(String... parts). Which reflective call passes "a" and "b" as the parts?

options.says: Cast to Object[], the array is spread into two arguments, "a" and "b", for a method that takes one parameter, so invoke throws IllegalArgumentException.
A List is not a String[], so invoke refuses it with IllegalArgumentException: the varargs parameter needs an actual array.
The varargs parameter is one String[] argument, and the cast keeps invoke from spreading the array over its own Object... parameter.

concepts: A static final or record field cannot be set by reflection, and a compile-time constant is inlined so changing it is invisible.
A varargs method invoked through reflection takes its variable arguments as one array argument.
